note: The E and A shapes together: the key's chord in both shapes on a caged-neck (moves: any key), then the 1st, 4th and 5th chords as barre chords in one area of the neck, once with the 1st chord in the E shape and once in the A shape. Those chord-shapes and strum-alongs are pinned to their key, since the lowest barre shape changes with the key; the chords are tokens, counted the long way once.

exercise.title: E and A shapes: one chord in two places, then three chords
exercise.why: The E shape has its root on the low E string and the A shape has it on the A string, so in one area of the neck the two shapes give you three chords of a key: the 1st, the 4th and the 5th.

cells.text:
Each row below is the chord of {{=key}} in one shape: the E shape, with its root on the low E string, then the A shape, with its root on the A string. Press Play on the CAGED / Chord panel of each row to hear it. Then play one shape and the other, and say which string holds the root each time.
Practice until you find the root of either shape without looking.
{{?key}}In another key both shapes slide along the neck, and the root stays on the low E string in the E shape and on the A string in the A shape.

cells.heading: Three chords from the E shape

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the three chords as barre chords in one area of the neck. {{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and here it is in the E shape. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th, built on {{5}}: both are in the A shape.
Then press Play under them to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}, and strum down on every beat.

cells.heading: Three chords from the A shape

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear three chords of another key as barre chords. Now {{chord:I}} is in the A shape, and {{chord:IV}} and {{chord:V}} are both in the E shape.
Then press Play under them to start the metronome, and strum down on every beat.
Practice until you see where {{chord:IV}} and {{chord:V}} are before you leave {{chord:I}}.
